Observed before fix: ai-offer-creation/quantity-break/translate-portal used 'dev_doc' near-uniformly; analytics/translate-offers used 'test_case' near-uniformly; ask-for-review/onboarding-dashboard used 'spec_doc' near-uniformly; _object-level/wholesale-pricing-offer/variant-swatches mixed po_dev_confirm/test_case. confirmation_source_type_convention_deci.decision: type = 'spec_doc' when confirmation_source.ref.authored_on == doc_set_generated_at fallback ('2026-10-01', i.e. the claim carries no claim-specific dated observation and is a general narrative statement of the feature/rule, closest to a QA-authored internal spec). type = 'test_case' when confirmation_source.ref.authored_on is any other specific date (i.e. the claim's authored_on was itself extracted from a dated live-verification/live-confirmation event in the source text — Playwright MCP session on store test-vl-1, or a dated decision-log entry recording a live-confirmed fact) — nearest fit among the 4 fixed §3 enum values per the operator's own suggested mapping, acknowledging it is an imperfect fit (no formal Testlane test-case ID/PASS-build record exists for these sessions).
confirmation_source_type_convention_deci.mechanism: Mechanical, auditable, applied uniformly by script across all 11 shards: for every kb_candidate with knowledge_kind=CONFIRMED_EXPECTED, set confirmation_source.type from confirmation_source.ref.authored_on per the rule above. Did NOT touch derivation, authored_by, authored_on, locator, url, quote, or any doc_refs[].type ('doc_ref' is an unrelated evidence-ref field, not confirmation_source.type). Did NOT touch knowledge_kind, confidence, or any item where confirmation_source is null (INFERRED/OBSERVED_CURRENT items unaffected).

derivation_consistency_fix.problem: While applying the confirmation_source.type convention fix, discovered a second cross-shard inconsistency: 4/11 shards (analytics, ask-for-review, variant-swatches, wholesale-pricing-offer) omitted confirmation_source.derivation entirely for their CONFIRMED_EXPECTED items, following a literal reading of contract §3 ('derivation chỉ áp cho type dev_doc'). The other 7 shards set derivation='prose' regardless of type. This matters because qa-checklist-builder's STRONG/BASELINE oracle brake ('Phanh derivation') checks confirmation_source.derivation == 'prose' on EVERY CONFIRMED_EXPECTED oracle item to grant STRONG, not just dev_doc-typed ones — leaving it absent would have silently capped every oracle in those 4 shards (118 CONFIRMED_EXPECTED items) at BASELINE regardless of actual claim strength, right as those shards feed into qa-checklist-builder next.
derivation_consistency_fix.decision: Set confirmation_source.derivation on every CONFIRMED_EXPECTED item from its own claim normativity, independent of confirmation_source.type — matching contract §3's own rule ('derivation phải khớp normativity của claim nguồn'): normativity EXPLICIT -> derivation='prose'; normativity IMPLIED_BY_CODE_ARTIFACT -> derivation='code_artifact'. Verified first (0 violations) that CONFIRMED_EXPECTED items only ever carry normativity EXPLICIT (327) or IMPLIED_BY_CODE_ARTIFACT (2) — never EXAMPLE_ONLY/HEDGED_RATIONALE, which would have been a gate violation requiring escalation rather than a mechanical fix.
derivation_consistency_fix.result: 329 CONFIRMED_EXPECTED items checked; 73 had derivation added (previously absent), 46 had a mismatched value corrected (all in analytics.json=24 and variant-swatches.json=21, where some items apparently had derivation explicitly set to null), 210 already matched. Final state: every CONFIRMED_EXPECTED item carries derivation, 100% consistent with its own normativity. Only the 2 known multibuy-mix-match-combo IMPLIED_BY_CODE_ARTIFACT items carry derivation='code_artifact' (correctly preserved as the weaker signal); all others carry 'prose'.
derivation_consistency_fix.script: scratchpad fix-derivation-consistency.mjs (ephemeral, logic fully reproduced in this manifest entry for audit).

oracle_strength_consistency_fix.problem: After all 10 qa-checklist-builder agents completed, discovered a third cross-shard inconsistency, directly downstream of fix #1: 9/10 checklists applied the literal contract oracle rule (knowledge_kind CONFIRMED_EXPECTED + confirmation_source.derivation=='prose' -> oracle_strength STRONG). The variant-swatches checklist-builder unilaterally re-litigated the orchestrator's own confirmation_source.type convention decision (fix #1) -- citing config/products/qik-volume.json's doc_input.source_repo note ('QA-authored, not dev-gen') as grounds to doubt that 'spec_doc' was the right type -- and blanket-capped ALL 33 of its checks at BASELINE/NONE regardless of actual derivation/knowledge_kind, flagging this explicitly as gate.conditions for reviewer attention rather than applying silently. That doubt is legitimate on its own terms, but re-litigating it at the checklist-builder layer, shard-by-shard, is exactly the kind of inconsistency this run's whole confirmation_source.type exercise exists to prevent (same root cause as fix #1) -- and it also runs directly against contract §3's stated purpose for DOC_BOOTSTRAP's default-flip rule ('nếu vẫn mặc định OBSERVED_CURRENT thì KB sinh ra không bao giờ dùng được làm expected result' -- i.e. capping everything at BASELINE defeats the explicit design intent of the mode).
oracle_strength_consistency_fix.decision: Recomputed oracle_strength independently and mechanically for every check in all 10 checklists (369 checks total) from the actual knowledge_kind + confirmation_source.derivation of each check's cited kb_id(s), resolved against the correct source shard (feature-level kb.json, or object-level kb.json for the 3 discount-offers features -- resolver handled 3 different ad-hoc prefixing conventions the checklist-builders independently invented for object-level refs: 'OBJ:KB-nnn', 'OBJ-KB-nnn', and bare 'KB-nnn' falling back to object-level when absent from the feature's own shard). Rule applied uniformly: any cited kb_id INFERRED/PROPOSED -> NONE; all cited kb_ids CONFIRMED_EXPECTED with derivation=='prose' -> STRONG; all CONFIRMED_EXPECTED but some derivation=='code_artifact' -> BASELINE (phanh derivation, preserves the 2 known weaker multibuy items); any cited kb_id OBSERVED_CURRENT (none INFERRED) -> BASELINE (preserves KNOWN_DEFECT regression-watch checks at BASELINE, e.g. variant-swatches' own storefront-rendering-bug checks, correctly never promoted). Where this disagreed with what a checklist-builder wrote, overrode oracle_strength and kept the status/READY vs NEEDS_CONFIRMATION invariant consistent (NONE always pairs with NEEDS_CONFIRMATION).
oracle_strength_consistency_fix.result: 369 checks examined across 10 shards, 0 unresolved kb_id references (resolver matched every ref including all 3 ad-hoc object-level prefix styles), 24 checks changed: variant-swatches 16 (STRONG 0->16, BASELINE 21->5, NONE unchanged at 12 -- the 5 remaining BASELINE checks are genuinely OBSERVED_CURRENT/KNOWN_DEFECT regression-watch items, correctly NOT promoted), translate-offers 4, analytics 2, quantity-break 2. The other 6 shards (multibuy-mix-match-combo, wholesale-pricing-offer, onboarding-dashboard, ai-offer-creation, translate-portal, ask-for-review) needed 0 changes -- already fully consistent with the rule.

fixes_applied.F-013_ROOT_CAUSE_CONFIRMED: Investigated per explicit operator instruction rather than patching the symptom a 3rd time. Confirmed via `xattr -l` (com.apple.file-provider-domain-id / com.apple.fileprovider.detached present on ~/Documents) and `brctl status` (active CloudDocs sync daemon) that this repo sits under a macOS File Provider domain (iCloud Drive 'Desktop & Documents Folders' sync). The actual bug: both round-1-3's shell-level `rm -rf OUT/*` AND round-3's own 'fix' (rmSync(OUT) inside the script) used the identical shape -- bulk-delete the whole publish-preview directory, then rapidly recreate ~70 files in it -- which is exactly the pattern that races the file-provider daemon into resurrecting a renamed, empty, auto-numbered duplicate of what it still had queued from before the delete (collision counter increments each time: ' 2' round 3, ' 3' round 4, because each 'fix' was the same race under a new name, not a different mechanism). ALSO discovered and fixed, while investigating this: a second, unrelated ordering bug in sanitizeText -- the generic agent-name/vocabulary substitution pass (added for F-010 in round 2, extended for F-015/F-016 in round 4) ran BEFORE the specific 'candidate/product-kb/_object-level.json -> the object-level KB' path regex (added for F-002 in round 1), so the generic '_object-level.json -> object-level KB' rule fired first and eat the filename out from under the more specific rule, leaving a dangling 'candidate/product-kb/' prefix behind in exactly 1 location (variant-swatches profile.json) -- this was caught by this round's own audit, not by context-quality-reviewer, and would have been a 5th review-round finding had it not been caught here.
fixes_applied.F-013_ACTUAL_FIX: Removed the whole-directory delete entirely from strip-to-publish-preview.mjs -- every write is now a pure overwrite-in-place (mkdirSync is idempotent, writeFileSync overwrites an existing file without an intervening delete), so there is never a moment where the destination directory doesn't exist for the file-provider daemon to 'resurrect'. Did a single one-time manual `rm -rf` of the whole publish-preview directory first (per operator instruction) to clear the pre-existing ' 3' duplicates from a clean slate, waited 10s for the filesystem to settle, then ran the regeneration pipeline 3 full times with no internal bulk-delete, checking for duplicates both immediately and after a 20-30s settle delay after each pass -- 0 duplicates in all 6 checks (3 passes x immediate+settled).
fixes_applied.F-013_ordering_fix: Moved the generic substitution pass (applyAgentNameSubstitutions) to run LAST in sanitizeText, after all specific path/ID regexes, in all 3 strip scripts -- fixes the ordering bug described above and prevents the same class recurring for any future generic rule.
